key_insight: Combining ECG and chest X-ray data in a multimodal deep learning model improved prediction of future moderate-to-severe regurgitant valvular heart disease, especially aortic regurgitation.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier risk stratification for large-scale screening when echocardiography is not practical for everyone.
method: Retrospective multicenter study of 212,888 paired ECG-CXR examinations from 116,380 patients.
Built a multimodal neural network with pretrained ECG and CXR encoders plus token-level cross-modal fusion.
Used a class-specific gating mechanism to adaptively combine ECG-only, CXR-only, and fused predictions.
evidence_signal: Across AR, MR, and TR, multimodal models outperformed unimodal models on C-index, AUROC, AUPRC, decision curve analysis, NRI, and Kaplan-Meier stratification in two Chinese centers.
watch_item: The findings come from retrospective data in two centers, so external validation and workflow testing are needed before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Multimodal Deep Learning Integrating Electrocardiography and Chest Radiography Enhances Prediction of Incident Regurgitant Valvular Heart Disease
